title: An element of a local projective module lies in a free summand
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring (a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal), let $P$ be a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and let $x\in P$. There exist submodules $G,H\subseteq P$ such that $P=G\oplus H$, $x\in G$, and $G$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Here $P=G\oplus H$ means that every element of $P$ has a unique expression $g+h$ with $g\in G$ and $h\in H$. No finite-generation hypothesis is imposed on $P$ or $G$.

proof.text: By the direct-summand characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], realize $P$ as a submodule of a free module $F$ with an $R$-linear retraction $\pi:F\to P$, $\pi|_P=1_P$. Put $Q=\ker\pi$; then $f=\pi(f)+(f-\pi(f))$ gives $F=P\oplus Q$. Choose a basis of $F$ as in [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. If $x=0$, take $G=0$, whose basis is empty, and $H=P$. Henceforth assume $x\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof: first sentence and the zero-element case

proof.text:
Among all bases of this fixed ambient module $F$, choose one $\mathcal B$ for which the finite support of $x$ has least cardinality $n$, using [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and the least-element property of $\mathbb N$. Enumerate this support by $e_1,\ldots,e_n$, so $x=\sum_i a_i e_i$. For every $j$, $a_j$ is not an $R$-linear combination of the other $a_i$. Indeed, if $a_j=\sum_{i
e j}a_i c_i$, replace $e_i$ by $e_i+c_i e_j$ for $i
e j$ in this finite support, and fix $e_j$ and the remaining basis vectors. The inverse replacement subtracts $c_i e_j$, so this is still a basis. In this basis $x=\sum_{i
e j}a_i(e_i+c_i e_j)$, with support at most $n-1$, contrary to the choice of $n$.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof: first paragraph, minimal support over all bases and elementary basis shear

proof.text: Put $y_i=\pi(e_i)\in P$. Split the basis coordinates of each $y_i$ as $y_i=\sum_{j=1}^n b_{ij}e_j+t_i$, with $t_i$ in the span of $\mathcal B\setminus\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}$, using [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Since $\pi(x)=x$, we have $x=\sum_i a_i y_i$. Comparing the $e_j$-coordinates gives $a_j=\sum_i a_i b_{ij}$ for every $j$.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof: second paragraph and the coefficient comparison in the last paragraph

proof.text:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be the unique maximal ideal of $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], the nonunits are exactly the elements of $\mathfrak m$. The relations in step 3 imply $1-b_{jj}$ is a nonunit: if it were a unit, $(1-b_{jj})a_j=\sum_{i
e j}a_i b_{ij}$ would express $a_j$ using the other coefficients, contradicting step 2. Thus $1-b_{jj}\in\mathfrak m$, so $b_{jj}
otin\mathfrak m$ (otherwise their sum $1$ lies in this proper ideal), and $b_{jj}$ is a unit. Likewise for $i
e j$, if $b_{ij}$ were a unit, the equality $b_{ij}a_i=(1-b_{jj})a_j-\sum_{k
e i,j}a_k b_{kj}$ would express $a_i$ using the other coefficients. Hence every off-diagonal $b_{ij}$ belongs to $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof: last paragraph, minimality forces unit diagonal and nonunit off-diagonal

proof.text: Let $A=(b_{ij})$. In the Leibniz formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], the identity permutation contributes the unit $u=\prod_i b_{ii}$. Every other permutation moves some index, so its product has an off-diagonal factor in $\mathfrak m$; its signed product is in $\mathfrak m$. Therefore $\det A=u+v$ with $v\in\mathfrak m$. If $\det A$ belonged to $\mathfrak m$, then $u=(\det A)-v$ would too, contradicting the unit criterion [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion]. Thus $\det A$ is a unit. The adjugate identities [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] show explicitly that $(\det A)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(A)$ is a two-sided inverse of $A$. This writes out the local matrix argument at the end of Tag 0592 without introducing a new lemma.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof: last sentence, determinant is a unit and adjugate gives inverse

proof.text: Let $E$ be the span of $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ and $T$ the span of the remaining original basis vectors; thus $F=E\oplus T$ by [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Define $U:F\to F$ by $U(e_i)=y_i$ and by fixing the other basis vectors. On a finite-coordinate vector $c=(c_i)$ and $t\in T$, its formula is $U(c,t)=(Cc,Dc+t)$, where $(Cc)_j=\sum_i b_{ij}c_i$ and $Dc=\sum_i c_i t_i$. The operator $C$ is the transpose of $A$ and has inverse the transpose of the inverse from step 5 (transpose reverses products by the entrywise formula). Consequently $(c,t)\mapsto(C^{-1}c,t-DC^{-1}c)$ is an inverse of $U$, as direct substitution verifies both composites. It follows from uniqueness of expansions in the old basis that $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ together with the remaining original basis vectors form a basis of $F$.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof: second paragraph, the basis replacement automorphism, with its inverse written out

proof.text: Let $G=\sum_i R y_i=U(E)$, which is contained in $P$, and keep $T$ from step 6. The new basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] gives $F=G\oplus T$ and makes $G$ finite free with basis $y_1,\ldots,y_n$. For each $p\in P$, write uniquely $p=g+t$ in this decomposition of $F$. Since $g\in G\subseteq P$, also $t=p-g\in P\cap T$. Conversely $G\cap(P\cap T)=0$, so $H=P\cap T$ gives $P=G\oplus H$. Finally $x=\sum_i a_i y_i\in G$ by step 3. Together with the zero case of step 1, these are all clauses of the item, without any finite-generation hypothesis on $P$.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof: second paragraph, the free submodule and its complement inside P
